gold: Withdrawn by the author after the discovery of substantive errors that invalidate the central results. The Weyl-sequence and weighted-resolvent argument does not distinguish the proposed inverse-cube curvature regime from the free operator, and the dimensional-scaling argument does not establish the claimed critical exponent
Withdrawn due to an error in the proof of Lemma 4.3 (Composition Lemma), which was based on the argument in arXiv:2202.03178v2

Withdrawn due to errors. Definition 3.2 forces every measure in the sampleable class to have full support on B_R, so D_C(mu) is bounded below by a positive constant for every mu and no Gaussian smoothing lies in the class. The convexification cost of Definition 3.6 is zero for every measure, so Theorem 3.7 is false. Theorem 4.8 and Proposition 4.10 are unproved and Theorem 5.3 is wrong

Withdrawn by the author because the identifiability result in Sections 3.3-3.4 is incorrect. Residual orthogonality depends only on the fitted sum and therefore cannot identify the convex-concave decomposition; the proof also incorrectly treats the difference of two concave functions as necessarily affine. A substantially revised manuscript is in preparation

Version 2 corrects an error in the statement of Theorem B that affected the proof, but not the statement, of Theorem A. The order of these results has now been swapped: the original Theorem B (now Theorem A) has been modified with a stronger hypothesis. The authors thank Luis Pablo Colmenar for pointing out the error. The journal version of this paper in J. Pure Appl. Algebra has been retracted
Withdrawn by the author due to a confound in stimulus assignment that invalidates the main results; addressing it requires re-running the experiment with matched stimuli

Withdrawn by the authors after identifying inconsistencies between the described adaptive curriculum and the implementation used to generate the reported experiments, particularly in the success-rate feedback mechanism and replay-weight schedule. These issues require the experiments and conclusions to be reevaluated

The author has identified substantive flaws in the theoretical arguments supporting the finite-horizon quantile calibration law and the matrix-gain regression result (Sections 3--4 and Supplementary Sections S2--S3). These flaws affect the paper's main conclusions, so the paper is withdrawn

Withdrawn by the authors. An audit of the simulation code found an error in the satellite beam-gain model (off-boresight angle computed incorrectly) and a non-standard clutter model, which together produced the reported urbanârural disparity. With these corrected, the main conclusions do not hold.

The paper is being withdrawn because one of the main statements concerning the TVD property of second-order methods for two-dimensional scalar conservation laws lacks sufficient conditions. A counterexample has been found showing that the claimed TVD property does not hold under the conditions stated in the paper. This affects the validity of the corresponding result and its conclusions

Withdrawn by the author because an error in the localization argument invalidates the proof of Theorem 1.1. The comparison between temporal growth and the size of the localized Cauchy data is not justified. The claimed Gevrey nonsolvability result is therefore withdrawn

Withdrawn due to an error in the analysis of shear flows near Couette: the weight v defined in (5.19) was incorrectly treated as self-adjoint in the energy identities. The results for the exact Couette flow are unaffected and were subsequently included, improved and extended in arXiv:2101.01696

Withdrawn due to factual errors. Sec. IV wrongly states that Inmon's data marts are normalised (3NF; they are typically dimensional) and dates Inmon's book to 1990 (it is 1992). The abstract misquotes Inmon's endorsement and wrongly claims Kimball and Inmon were not rivals. Figs. 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 8 and 9 reproduce third-party material. Please do not cite this version

Withdrawn by the authors after identifying an implementation error in adapter coefficient scaling that materially affects the main empirical results and invalidates the current conclusions. A corrected reanalysis is in progress

The core claim that the simulation becomes reactive does not hold, even though the findings on its effects on the ego vehicle remain valid. This claim was re-evaluated based on reviewer feedback, and the paper is therefore being retracted. However, the valid results regarding the effects on the ego vehicle are being merged into the parallel study: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.23393

Withdrawn by the author due to critical issues identified in the experimental methodology and dataset structure: the reported negative transfer and optimization penalties were found to be artifacts of data leakage and lack of headroom over trivial lookup baselines, and the main findings failed to generalize to an external benchmark (JARVIS-DFT)

v3: correction. A leakage audit found four defects in the v2 feature construction; on the corrected panel a persistence forecast (MAE 5.79 pp) significantly beats XGBoost (6.55 pp, p = 0.001) and the v2 claim of an 85.3% improvement is withdrawn. See the Correction notice. Code and corrected panel: github.com/TanvirTurja/amr-forecasting-rag ; full reanalysis under journal review

Withdrawn by the author after the discovery of substantive errors in the main argument. In particular, the purported critical example does not establish the claimed sharp r^--3 curvature-decay threshold, and several compactness and gauge estimates used in the proof are invalid. These issues undermine the principal conclusions of the paper

Withdrawn by the authors due to methodological flaws in the benchmark construction and evaluation pipeline: specifically, model overlap between the multi-LLM silver-annotation pool (Section 3.3) and the evaluated models (Section 4), as well as cross-split context leakage from bidirectional dialogue expansion (Section 3.2), which invalidate the reported experimental results and conclusions

Withdrawn by the author Sarat Moka: the proof of Theorem 2 is incorrect. The resampling set constructed in Section 4 is not that of the general partial rejection sampling algorithm of Guo, Jerrum and Liu (STOC 2017), so their Theorem 4.5 does not apply and exactness of the proposed algorithm is not established. Theorems 3, 5 and 6, which depend on Theorem 2, are likewise unproven
Withdrawn due to an error in the proof of Lemma 3.10 (Composition Lemma), which was based on the argument in arXiv:2202.03178v2

Withdrawn due to inconsistencies identified during verification of the theoretical framework. Specifically, the treatment of the environment modes in Eq. 6 and an incorrectly normalised state in Eq. 8. Correcting this significantly changes the results and the reported sensing advantage no longer occurs for measuring WGM resonance shifts

Withdrawn by the author. The experiments lack length controls to isolate cross-lingual transfer from the effect of shortening on detection. The paper also lacks semantic or quality preservation metrics under the transformation and does not demonstrate that output remains useful. As a result, the central claim that cross-lingual summarization outperforms prior attacks is not adequately supported.

10 pages, 2 figures. v2 is a substantial correction: v1's main result and mechanism claim are withdrawn. v1 compared against an interpolated, never-executed fixed-cadence baseline; running it erases the effect. Four pre-registered controls, asserted in v1 as passing, were unimplemented; all now run, and budget parity fails. Code: https://github.com/samyama-ai/updatable-graph-index

This paper has been withdrawn by the author due to a fundamental mathematical error in the similarity construction of Section 3 and the subsequent Bochner integration in Section 4. Specifically, the induced norm makes the transmutation operator an isometry, which prevents the deformed semigroup from acquiring the claimed additional decay required for the convergence of the non-local integrals

Withdrawn after identifying an evaluation-window mismatch: the reported validation and test evaluations skip the first 336 target positions, making comparisons with cited baselines non-equivalent. This is not data leakage. Corrected evaluation preserves nontrivial forecasting behavior, but changes some benchmark results. A revised version may follow

Withdrawn by the author: the K-matrix used for the nu=2/3 state is incorrect, and the Bogoliubov-de Gennes results and numerical experimental signatures derived from it, which run through the whole paper, are therefore wrong. A corrected and substantially different analysis is given in arXiv:2610.01486

18 pages, 2 figures, 5 tables. Version 2 corrects version 1: its PlotQA scores used the wrong axis for most items; DePlot is now scored on the same ChartX items as the VLMs; the claim that every VLM beat DePlot on both benchmarks is withdrawn (all nine lead it in aggregate on six ChartX chart types only). See Section 7. Code and results: https://github.com/tommycarstensen/plotpick-validation

Withdrawn because key empirical claims in v1, including the 27-building result, MAE=3.07 m, and 5.0-5.5 m error/uncertainty bounds, were not supported by the archived source data and released implementation. A gap was identified in the proof of the theorem asserting the topological invariance of multiplicity one. Consequently, the theorem has been withdrawn from this version
The proof of Lemma 5 contains a gap, and it is unclear whether the statement of the lemma itself is true. Since the main results depend on this lemma, the paper is withdrawn

Withdrawn because Section 4.2 contains a substantive error in the proof of the main theorem: Eq. (11) incorrectly drops the query key (k_i) when applying the data processing inequality. The positivity condition used in Eqs. (6) and (14) is also insufficient. These errors invalidate the main theorem

Major correction. The previously claimed final PP+not-AC construction is withdrawn. The package forcing targets right inverses, a stronger splitting principle incompatible with the intended seed preservation; the non-well-orderability and limit-stage SVC arguments also fail. The corrected manuscript retains the Cohen symmetric seed result and records the superseded approach

The gauge field of the hyperbolic mode is nearly longitudinal. Instead of the Coulomb gauge we had treated it in the Weyl gauge. However, since the electron Green's function is gauge dependent, quantities like Z needs to be treated carefully and the expressions given in the paper are incorrect. This paper is being withdrawn and will be replaced later by one where these issues will be discussed

12 pages. Complete rewrite of v1, new title. Withdrawn as erroneous: the Hermitian Schur-state definition (Def. 4), the Schur-product identity (Prop. 10), and the tree-counting results (Thm. 26, Cor. 28, 36). No result of v1 is used

v2: 53 pages, 7 figures. Substantial revision and extension; title changed. See "Changes from version 1" in the manuscript. Code: github.com/hecboar/linear-readout-threshold-recovery
In all the five versions of the manuscript, the definition of radiated energy in equation (9), on which much of the rest of the paper is based, is incorrect and thus the paper has been withdrawn

Withdrawn due to errors in Sections 3.3--3.4 and 4.2 of arXiv:2512.11877v4. The stated assumptions do not establish the canonical interpolation or $\tilde G=2P$. A physics-oriented reformulation examining the conditions for continuous black-hole information recovery is being prepared for hep-th

16 pages. v2 is a major revision with a new title (v1: "Pair correlation: Variations on a theme"). This version treats only pair correlation for sums of two ordinates, proving a stronger and more uniform asymptotic than the corresponding case mu=2 of v1. The proofs of Theorems 1.2 and 1.3 of v1 for general mu contain gaps, and those statements are withdrawn. Comments welcome

Withdrawn due to a counterexample identified after posting that invalidates a key step in the risk-averse regret bounds. The result does not hold as stated under the assumptions given. We are revising the analysis and will resubmit if the fix can be established rigorously

v4: scope narrowed to the theory. The benchmark study of v1-v3 is withdrawn: a scoring error counted a run with no alarm as a detection, inflating the proposed method only. Theory and proofs stand. Withdrawn due to errors identified in the derivation of the Langevin evolution equation (dimensional inconsistencies and an error in the centrality-scaling ansatz) that require revision of the model

Withdrawn by the authors because an error in the derivation leading to Eq. (16) invalidates the principal quantitative conclusions of the manuscript

Withdrawn because key empirical claims in v1, including the 27-building result, MAE=3.07 m, and 5.0-5.5 m error/uncertainty bounds, were not supported by the archived source data and released implementation. The authors withdraw the paper to correct the scientific record. A substantially redesigned study will be submitted separately

This paper has been withdrawn by the author due to a fundamental mathematical error in the similarity construction of Section 3 and the subsequent Bochner integration in Section 4. Specifically, the induced norm makes the transmutation operator an isometry, which prevents the deformed semigroup from acquiring the claimed additional decay required for the convergence of the non-local integrals

Withdrawn by the author because an error in the localization argument invalidates the proof of Theorem 1.1. The comparison between temporal growth and the size of the localized Cauchy data is not justified. The claimed Gevrey nonsolvability result is therefore withdrawn

Withdrawn by the authors due to methodological flaws in the benchmark construction and evaluation pipeline: specifically, model overlap between the multi-LLM silver-annotation pool (Section 3.3) and the evaluated models (Section 4), as well as cross-split context leakage from bidirectional dialogue expansion (Section 3.2), which invalidate the reported experimental results and conclusions

Withdrawn due to a counterexample identified after posting that invalidates a key step in the risk-averse regret bounds. The result does not hold as stated under the assumptions given. We are revising the analysis and will resubmit if the fix can be established rigorously

The gauge field of the hyperbolic mode is nearly longitudinal. Instead of the Coulomb gauge we had treated it in the Weyl gauge. However, since the electron Green's function is gauge dependent, quantities like Z needs to be treated carefully and the expressions given in the paper are incorrect. This paper is being withdrawn and will be replaced later by one where these issues will be discussed

Withdrawn after identifying an evaluation-window mismatch: the reported validation and test evaluations skip the first 336 target positions, making comparisons with cited baselines non-equivalent. This is not data leakage. Corrected evaluation preserves nontrivial forecasting behavior, but changes some benchmark results. A revised version may follow

Withdrawn due to factual errors. Sec. IV wrongly states that Inmon's data marts are normalised (3NF; they are typically dimensional) and dates Inmon's book to 1990 (it is 1992). The abstract misquotes Inmon's endorsement and wrongly claims Kimball and Inmon were not rivals. Figs. 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 8 and 9 reproduce third-party material. Please do not cite this version

10 pages, 2 figures. v2 is a substantial correction: v1's main result and mechanism claim are withdrawn. v1 compared against an interpolated, never-executed fixed-cadence baseline; running it erases the effect. Four pre-registered controls, asserted in v1 as passing, were unimplemented; all now run, and budget parity fails. Code: https://github.com/samyama-ai/updatable-graph-index

Withdrawn by the author because the manuscript contains substantial theoretical errors in several core arguments and derivations, affecting the validity of multiple central claims. These problems require a comprehensive reassessment, and no corrected version is currently available. Readers should not rely on or cite this version

This note is withdrawn due to a flaw in Lemma 3.3 of "Exotic Dehn twists and homotopy coherent group actions" by S. Kang, J. Park, and M. Taniguchi (see the erratum on the authors' websites). The proof of our main result relies crucially on this lemma and is thus no longer valid
Withdrawn due to errors identified in the derivation of the Langevin evolution equation (dimensional inconsistencies and an error in the centrality-scaling ansatz) that require revision of the model
Withdrawn by the authors due to an evaluation error: some Pass@8 values in Table 1 were computed on incomplete task sets. The affected comparisons will be revised

The author has identified substantive flaws in the theoretical arguments supporting the finite-horizon quantile calibration law and the matrix-gain regression result (Sections 3--4 and Supplementary Sections S2--S3). These flaws affect the paper's main conclusions, so the paper is withdrawn

v2: Adds an adaptive-attacker evaluation in which Ring 1 is fully evaded (500/500 documents, three corpora); scales to the full NQ, HotpotQA and MS-MARCO corpora; corrects Proposition 1, whose boundary is corpus-dependent (0.214/0.251/0.558) not 0.5; retracts a proposed closed form after a pre-registered prediction failed. The v1 headline 91%-to-13% result is withdrawn

This paper is withdrawn due to a gap in the proof of Lemma 3.3 of "Exotic Dehn twists and homotopy coherent group actions", which also affects Proposition 3.5 used in the present paper. The main theorem of the present paper remains valid, and a completely different proof will be presented in forthcoming work

This paper is being withdrawn as we have been informed by Dr Viraj Karambelkar (Columbia University) and colleagues that the ring we have reported around VY CMa is an artifact. The results reported in our paper are therefore invalid. We are very grateful to Dr Karambelkar for drawing our attention to this matter in a timely fashion

Replaces the withdrawn version 1; Version 1 reported causality violations of GW on Hubbard clusters; these came from a sign error in the polarization of the accompanying code and are withdrawn.
